question: What are the two main components that make up the cardiovascular system?
explanation: The cardiovascular system is composed of the heart, which acts as the pump, and blood vessels, which serve as the delivery pipes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do the cells in our body constantly need blood flowing to them?

options.A: To produce white blood cells directly inside the tissue spaces
options.B: To keep blood pressure at zero in the outer extremities
options.C: To deliver oxygen and nutrients while removing waste products
options.D: To cool down the internal organs by releasing sweat locally

explanation: Think of blood as the body's ultimate delivery and sanitation service! Cells need a steady supply of oxygen and food to survive, and they produce waste that must be carried away.

question: Which layer of the heart wall does the actual hard work of pumping blood?
explanation: The myocardium is made of strong muscle tissue. Every time your heart beats, it's the myocardium doing the heavy lifting to push blood out!

question: What is the main job of the fluid found inside the protective sac around the heart (pericardium)?

options.A: To store extra blood volume during times of heavy exercise
options.B: To provide extra oxygen directly to the outer heart muscle
options.C: To reduce friction as the heart beats against surrounding tissues
options.D: To prevent electrical signals from leaving the heart wall

explanation: Your heart beats thousands of times a day without stopping! The pericardial fluid acts like a slippery lubricant so the heart can glide smoothly inside the chest without irritation.

question: Which heart chamber pumps oxygen-rich blood out into the main body artery (the aorta)?
explanation: The left ventricle is the powerhouse of the heart! It has the thickest walls because it has to push blood all the way around the entire body.

question: What is the main function of the heart valves during the cardiac cycle?

options.A: To prevent blood from flowing backward
options.B: To generate electrical sparks for the heartbeat
options.C: To filter bacteria out of the bloodstream
options.D: To separate the left and right lungs

explanation: Valves act like one-way doors that open to let blood pass forward and snap shut to stop it from flowing backward. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h3)

question: Where do the coronary arteries, which feed the heart muscle itself, take their origin?
explanation: The heart works non-stop, so it needs its own private blood supply! The coronary arteries branch off right at the base of the aorta to get the very first taste of fresh oxygen.

question: A patient has a sudden blockage in a main coronary artery. What is the immediate danger to the heart?

options.A: The heart valves will instantly turn inside out from lack of pressure.
options.B: The cardiac conduction system will stop making red blood cells.
options.C: The heart muscle supplied by that artery will be starved of oxygen and may die.
options.D: The lungs will immediately fill with air instead of blood.

explanation: When a coronary artery gets blocked, the heart muscle cells downstream lose their oxygen supply. If it's not fixed quickly, that part of the muscle gets damaged—this is what we call a heart attack.

question: What is the name of the natural pacemaker that sets the rhythm for the heart?
explanation: The Sinoatrial (SA) node is the boss of heart rhythms! It fires off electrical signals the fastest, keeping the whole heart beating in a steady, regular pattern.

question: Why does the electrical signal pause briefly at the AV node before heading down to the ventricles?

options.A: To let the heart take a quick rest between beats
options.B: To send extra blood back up into the lungs
options.C: To give the ventricles enough time to fill completely with blood
options.D: To measure the exact blood pressure inside the atria

explanation: That tiny pause is super important! It ensures the top chambers (atria) finish squeezing all their blood down into the bottom chambers before the ventricles pump it away.

question: What causes the first heart sound, commonly heard as 'lub'?
explanation: The first heart sound (S1) is produced when the tricuspid and mitral valves snap shut at the start of ventricular contraction. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is happening inside the heart chambers during diastole?

options.A: The ventricles squeeze blood into the arteries
options.B: The electrical signals stop moving entirely
options.C: The chambers relax and fill with blood

explanation: Diastole is the resting phase! The heart muscle relaxes so that blood can flow in and fill up the chambers, getting ready for the next big squeeze.

question: Which formula is used to calculate cardiac output?

options.B: Stroke volume multiplied by heart rate
options.D: Heart rate divided by stroke volume

explanation: Cardiac output is the product of how much blood is pumped per beat (stroke volume) and how many beats occur per minute (heart rate). [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h7)

question: If a patient's blood pressure drops suddenly, how does the body try to fix it right away?

options.B: Widespread widening of all blood vessels
options.C: A major decrease in the overall heart rate
options.D: Tightening blood vessels and speeding up the heart

explanation: To protect vital organs when pressure drops, the nervous system acts fast: it squeezes blood vessels (vasoconstriction) and makes the heart beat faster to keep blood moving!

question: Which blood vessels have walls that are only one cell thick for easy exchange of nutrients and gases?
explanation: Capillaries are the tiniest blood vessels. Because their walls are just one cell thick, oxygen and nutrients can easily slip out to feed your tissues while waste slips in.

question: Why do the veins in your limbs have one-way valves inside them?

options.A: To filter out dangerous toxins before blood enters the lungs
options.B: To store extra blood volume when a person is resting
options.C: To speed up blood flow as it leaves the left ventricle
options.D: To help push blood upward against gravity back toward the heart

explanation: Getting blood from your toes back up to your chest is a tough uphill battle against gravity! Vein valves act like little trapdoors that stop blood from sliding backward.
